stories.title: Public sector unions plan 24-hour strike for 12 November
stories.summary: Unions have announced plans for a 24-hour public sector strike on Thursday 12 November over delays in agreeing a new pay deal. The Public Services Committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions met today and, following the meeting, it said the Government has yet to make a credible offer to resolve the current dispute. Talks on a public sector pay deal were adjourned without agreement on Friday night. Union leaders met today to discuss their response. Lead union negotiator Kevin Callinan said there was a lot of anger in the room at the meeting which quickly turned into quiet determination. Unions were originally going to discuss plans for a strike on Wednesday 11 November but the work stoppage will now be held on the following day. This will coincide with the first of two meetings of European leaders due to take place next week as part of Ireland's EU Presidency.

stories.title: Oil drops 6% as Iran signals openness to peace talks
stories.summary: Oil fell about 6% today as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on ending the US-Israeli war with Iran lifted hopes for reduced Middle East supply disruptions, while Iran's president said the supreme leader had granted the government "certain authorities" regarding peace talks. Iranian negotiators held days of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at ending the war with the United States, and a draft proposal is being circulated with a follow-up meeting possible, an official briefed on the talks said on Monday. Brent crude futures fell $6.78, or 6.0%, to $106.65 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down $6.37, or 6.1%, at $97.75. The contracts fell as low as $105.86 and $97.12, respectively, after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government certain authorities for peace talks, boosting expectations of a diplomatic breakthrough, analysts said. Pezeshkian added Tehran "will try to resolve the problem with dialogue", without elaborating, according to state media. Brent ended October at its highest in six months on concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate again after tomorrow's US midterm elections.

stories.title: Coleman 'still thinking about' staying on with Ireland
stories.summary: Séamus Coleman is still keeping the door open on a return to action at club and international level. The 38-year-old, currently without a club, was not included in Heimir Hallgrimsson's UEFA Nations League squad for the quartet of matches in September and October. The indications at the time were that Coleman was on the lookout for a new club in order to prolong his chances of being involved at Euro 2028. Hallgrimsson has shared how keen he is on keeping Coleman in his plans. However the former Everton captain's comments in recent weeks have cast doubt on that possibility. Last week in conversation with Jamie Carragher on the The Overlap Fan Debate, Coleman hinted that he was leaning towards retirement, saying: "I don't want to completely draw a line in the sand, as I said I've been keeping fit. But it's edging towards that way - and happily as well." On Monday, Coleman appeared as a pundit for Sky Sports' coverage of Newcastle United v Everton with speculation rife that he was about to confirm his retirement. Instead, he underlined his stance that nothing has been decided.

stories.title: John Malkovich: 'Nobody liked my Irish accent!'
stories.summary: Actor John Malkovich has joked about how his attempt at an Irish accent in his new movie Wild Horse Nine fell flat with Irish members of the film crew and director Martin McDonagh. Set shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film by the In Bruges and Banshees of Inisherin writer and film maker sees Malkovich play Chris Carlisle, a jaded CIA agent who takes a break from destabilising the Chilean government and is dispatched to Easter Island with his partner Lee Chesterfield (Sam Rockwell). This odd couple spend most of the time driving around in a battered old coupe (the coup comes later) and bickering as they visit the island's famous monolithic statues while discussing the nature of the dirty work they carry out on behalf of the US government. Chris, who is also riddled with Catholic guilt and terminal cancer, is seeking to salve his conscious after a lifetime of covert activity by writing his tell-all memoirs. As he says to Lee at one point, "I was killing people before you were born." Meanwhile, back in the Chilean capital of Santiago, Steve Buscemi as bureau chief MJ is slowly losing his mind as he worries that lose cannon Chris is about to betray everyone. It’s classic McDonagh stuff. Quirky and absurd, what seems like a classic shaggy dog story develops into a reverie on recurrent themes from the Anglo-Irish director, such as stunted morality, guilt, redemption, and men’s basic inability to communicate with each other.

stories.title: Miriam O'Callaghan: 'I feel like I've won the lotto'
stories.summary: With no intention of slowing down, Miriam O'Callaghan is adding a new documentary to her busy work schedule. In the two-part show, Ireland’s Population Crash, the veteran broadcaster takes a look at the forces creating the country’s birth rate decline. She talks to Janice Butler about gratitude for her own children, her can-do attitude, and being a force for women in the workplace. "I had something on earlier," she explains why she’s dressed up. "I’m busy, always busy," she laughs. While she may have had something on, Miriam always looks well, part of her brand and general outlook on life: if she looks well, she feels well. It’s something she wrote about in her memoir, Life, Work, Everything, published last year. "I like to look well for myself. I love clothes and glamour. And why not? You can be glamorous and intelligent – they’re not mutually exclusive, as we now know," she laughs. Being in her 60s, she’s regularly asked about retirement, but she’s going nowhere. In fact, she’s as busy as ever with Prime Time, her weekend radio show and now a new documentary, Ireland’s Population Crash, a two-parter that explores the forces behind collapsing birth rates and shifting demographics that are quietly transforming the Ireland we thought we knew. "I totally respect people who want to retire. I don’t even like the thought of it; the idea of it is like retiring from life," she laughs. "There are 24 hours in every day, and I live life to the full, always have, always will. I find every day exciting. I’d say I’m very annoying to live with – they don’t say I am, but I’m sure I am."

stories.title: Carla Lockhart resigns from DUP after Drumcree dispute
stories.summary: Upper Bann MP Carla Lockhart has announced she has resigned from the DUP over its handling of the fallout from the Drumcree parading dispute, and is to sit as an independent unionist in the House of Commons. Carla Lockhart's resignation was widely expected after a clash with the DUP leadership over its failure to remove Sinn Féin's Michelle O'Neill from her role as First Minister. Ms Lockhart believes Ms O'Neill can no longer serve as First Minister due to her participation in a protest the PSNI deemed unlawful against an Orange Order Drumcree parade in Portadown last month. Ms O'Neill and several of her party colleagues are being investigated by police for taking part in the protest on the Garvaghy Road that was staged to prevent the parade proceeding through the predominantly nationalist area. Watch: Northern Editor Vincent Kearney analyses Carla Lockhart's resignation from the DUP The MP had called on her party to withdraw its deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly from her office - a move that would automatically force Ms O'Neill from her role.

stories.title: Tesco held talks to buy up to 150 Poundland shops - PA
stories.summary: Tesco has held talks over proposals to buy up to 150 Poundland stores amid the impending break-up of the high street discount chain. The UK's largest supermarket approached the chain’s owner over a possible move to buy as many as a quarter of Poundland’s UK and Ireland stores, sources with knowledge of the process have told the Press Association. Poundland uses the brand name Dealz in Ireland with 70 stores across the country. It is not clear how many of the shops discussed in the reported deal are in Ireland. It comes as Poundland bosses prepare to meet UK Government ministers later this week amid concerns that the retailer will be broken up despite a solvent takeover move being tabled. Poundland filed a notice to appoint administrators last week, putting the future of its roughly 11,000 workers at risk. The notice of intention to appoint administrators filed on Thursday gave the business 10 working days of breathing space from creditors to secure a potential rescue deal.

stories.title: Barry grabs only goal as Everton defeat 10-man Newcastle
stories.summary: Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James’ Park. Following a first half lacking in clear-cut opportunities, the Toffees took the lead shortly after the restart when Barry stabbed home his fourth league goal of the campaign. A frustrating night soured further for the Magpies as they finished the game with 10 men when substitute Jacob Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession at the death. Everton ended a three-game winless run in the Premier League, while Newcastle slip to 13th in the table. Monday’s match took place just four days after Everton’s 3-1 win over Newcastle in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and both sides made two changes to their starting XI as Anthony Elanga and Joelinton came in for the Magpies, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong lined up for the visitors. Harvey Barnes looked lively on the left flank for the hosts, sending a curling shot wide before his looping cross floated narrowly past the far post and Jordan Pickford was forced to hold Will Osula's deflected cross from a tight angle.

stories.title: Claudia Winkleman says she initially turned down Traitors
stories.summary: Presenter Claudia Winkleman has revealed she initially turned down her role hosting The Traitors when she was first offered the job. The 54-year-old former Strictly Come Dancing presenter has hosted four series of the BBC reality game show as well as two celebrity editions, but she rejected the role before being persuaded to watch the original Dutch series, which changed her mind. She told Harper's Bazaar: "I'm always in bed at 9pm with my book, but I started watching, and at midnight, I sent her (an unnamed TV executive) a text saying, 'I'll buy my own ticket'." Winkleman left Strictly, which she presented alongside Tess Daly, in 2025, and launched a BBC One celebrity chat show, The Claudia Winkleman Show, in December of that year. However, the London-born star said she did not want to do another series of the chat show. She continued: "The BBC wanted me to give it a go. Maybe, I thought, let's try something different? But never again. That's it. It wasn't for me.

stories.title: Twixmas travel: Where to go to escape the chaos of Christmas
stories.summary: Communications Consultant and Travel Enthusiast Lisa Regan shares her travel ideas for breaking up the 'Twixmas' period by taking a break to cities like Paris, Copenhagen, Tallinn or London. Listen back above. For many of us, the hustle and bustle of Christmas is all part of the charm, while for others it is potentially the most overwhelming time of the year. Regan is one of those people, and for the last few years she has been jetting off to destinations like Costa Rica, Mexico and Panama to escape the carnage. "I always go futher afield", she tells Brendan O'Connor. "It's just not my time to shine, I'm not into Christmas so I like to go [somewhere] warm and just get a total break from everything that's going on and all the shopping and all the antics." She recalls that when she first started going abroad for Christmas there was "a lot of questioning as to why". "It seemed a bit groundbreaking, but I think throughout the years more and more people have dipped their toe to try it themselves or they've heard of more people doing it so now I don't seem as out there when I'm travelling at Christmas time." stories.title: Republicans, Democrats make closing pitches in midterms
stories.summary: Democrats have sought to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican. It comes as President Donald Trump further pressed his legal efforts to intervene in ballot-counting as both parties ⁠made their closing arguments a day before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church. The race is critical to Democrats' hopes of ending the 53-47 Senate majority hold of Mr Trump's Republicans in the vote. Ms Stevens' surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state. An undeterred Mr Trump, who has been holding daily rallies around the country for Republican candidates, filed an emergency request with the US Supreme Court to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

stories.title: New electric car registrations continue to power upwards
stories.summary: New figures from the Society of the Irish Motor Industry show a 55% jump in the number of new electric cars registered during the month of October. Today's SIMI figures show that 1,092 new electric cars (battery electric cars) were registered, up from 706 registrations in October 2025. So far this year, a total of 36,270 new electric cars have been registered, which marks a 57% increase from the same month last year when 23,082 electric cars were registered. Overall new car registrations for October were up 15% to 2,501 from 2,180 in October of last year. Registrations year to date are up 6% to 130,754 on the same time last year when a total of 123,855 new cars were registered. Today's figures also reveal a 15% hike in Imported Used Cars, with the number registered rising to 7,831 in October compared to 6,791 in October last year. Year to date imports are up 32% to 79,969 from 60,452 the same time last year.

stories.title: 8 ways to fix your erratic sleep schedule
stories.summary: New research suggests that an irregular bedtime could have implications for your heart health. Researchers analysed sleep data from more than 10,000 adults who wore activity-tracking devices as part of the National Institutes of Health’s All of Us research programme. The findings revealed that variations in sleep timing from one night to the next over a six-month period were associated with a 20-23% increased risk of serious cardiovascular problems, including heart attacks, strokes and heart failure. Meanwhile, a greater number of complete sleep cycles each night was associated with a 28% lower risk of atrial arrhythmia, a common type of irregular heartbeat. However, unusually long sleep cycles were linked to a 55% higher risk of heart attack or stroke. With growing evidence highlighting the importance of consistent sleep habits, we spoke to Adele Crow, clinical lead occupational therapist at Cygnet Health Care, who shared her expert advice on how to get an erratic sleep schedule back on track. "Try and stick to a realistic time to wake up every day that works for you," advises Crow. stories.title: WC sell-off documents to be shared with FIFA Council
stories.summary: Confidential documents linked to Gianni Infantino's hugely controversial World Cup private investor plan will be made available for members of the FIFA Council to view. Infantino had sought to set up a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run the commercial interests of the World Cup and its other competitions, with private investors holding a minority stake. The plan was abandoned in August after three continental confederations rejected it and UEFA threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions. A letter sent by UEFA on behalf of European members of the FIFA Council on 19 October demanded answers to a series of questions about FFE and a range of other concerns about Infantino's presidency by Monday. It's understood FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom wrote to all Council members on Monday inviting them to view key documents related to the FFE proposal. Council members - including FIFA vice-presidents such as UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin - have been invited to register their interest within the next two weeks should they wish to view the documents, in person and under specific conditions, at FIFA's headquarters in Zurich.

"We would like to thank our customers for their patience and understanding," it added Earlier, Musgrave confirmed that the cyber incident was limited to a specific model of refrigeration. It said it was monitoring systems alerted them to the issue and immediate action was taken. It said that as a precaution, chilled and frozen products in the affected stores were removed from sale, and all other products remain available as normal.

stories.title: McCabe makes shortlist for FIFPRO Women's World 11
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland captain Katie McCabe has made the 26-player shortlist for the FIFPRO Women's World 11, the only global football award decided exclusively by professional players A total of 6,511 women’s footballers from 64 countries vote for their team of the year, with McCabe in the running to become the first Irish player - male or female - to make the final XI. Contenders are judged on their performances from 4 August 2025 to 16 August 2026 inclusive. McCabe had a stellar campaign with Arsenal last season, helping the Gunners to a second-placed finish in the WSL before moving to Chelsea in the summer. She was also central to Ireland's excellent World Cup qualification campaign, which saw them beat Poland (twice) and the Netherlands. Last April, Ireland boss Carla Ward described the Dubliner as "the best left-back in the world". The 11 players who receive the most votes in their position are selected on the Women’s World 11, which will be revealed in a week's time.

stories.title: Ex-rugby international pleads not guilty to perfume theft
stories.summary: Former Irish rugby international Brendan Mullin has pleaded not guilty to stealing a high-end fragrance from Brown Thomas on Dublin's Grafton Street. The ex-rugby player, who won 55 Irish caps between 1984 and 1995 before moving into financial services, is accused of the theft of Hermès perfume worth €158 on 15 May last. He faced his fifth hearing on this charge when he appeared before Judge John Hughes at Dublin District Court. Mr Mullin, aged 62, represented himself because of the ongoing legal aid reform dispute which has led many solicitors to withdraw from District Court cases. When his case was called, Mr Mullin greeted the judge and said: "My solicitor cannot be here obviously because of the ongoing dispute." "I am seeking a hearing date at District Court level, and pleading not guilty," he added.

stories.title: Israeli opposition meets, Netanyahu says voters back him
stories.summary: Party heads in the Israeli opposition camp, led by Gadi Eisenkot, will meet tomorrow after they all endorsed him for prime minister, while incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu has called for a broad coalition government under his leadership. It will be the diverse opposition grouping's first meeting since last week's close-fought election delivered no majority for either camp. Mr Eisenkot's Yashar party said the leaders of the so-called change bloc would meet "to discuss coordinating the bloc's next steps" in Herzliya tomorrow morning. His bloc won 48 seats while Mr Netanyahu's camp secured 53, of which 27 are from his Likud party. Arab-majority lists won a record 19 seats in the 120-member parliament, making them potential kingmakers. Mr Netanyahu called for a "broad national government" without the Arab parties, and said that as the head of the largest party, he should lead the next coalition.

stories.title: Iran says peace talks continuing despite no breakthrough
stories.summary: Contacts between Iran and the United States to end their eight-month war are continuing, Tehran has said, after days of Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough. "Consultations through mediators are very intensive. We have presented our conditions and proposals and everything depends on the political rationality of Washington," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in comments carried by state media outlet IRNA. Amid fears the conflict could reignite after tomorrow's midterm elections in the United States, China and Russia both spoke out on against the possibility of renewed military action in a war that has hit the global economy. While oil prices fell nearly 4% on hopes that the latest round of mediation could lead to a diplomatic solution to the crisis, Iranian sources said they believed a new US attack was still more likely than a deal. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the plan Iran had submitted in September to end the war remained the focus of discussions, but he confirmed comments attributed to Mr Araghchi on Saturday that the proposal could be shortened. "The basis of dialogue and talks between Iran and the US via mediators is still Iran's seven-step proposal, which is now condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days," he said.

stories.title: O'Sullivan secures first silverware with Gotham
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Denise O'Sullivan has claimed her fourth National Women's Soccer League Shield, and first with Gotham FC, after the New York-based side topped the league on Sunday. Gotham just needed a draw to secure enough points to win the title but went one better and defeated Utah Royals 2-0. Former Chelsea ace Guro Reiten kicked off the scoring with United States international Jaedyn Shaw getting their second late in the second half. "League champions. Truly deserved for an incredible group of people from top to bottom," O'Sullivan said on social media. O'Sullivan started the game and played all 90 minutes. Her performance was pivotal to their success with much of the play flowing through her and Savannah McCaskill in midfield. She previously won three league titles with North Carolina Courage who she played with for nine seasons. Gotham will now enter the post-season where they will face Seattle Reign in the NWSL Championship quarter-finals. This is the first Shield that Gotham have won but they have secured two of the past three Championships.

stories.title: Man told to leave house months before pensioner's death
stories.summary: A man who is accused of suffocating and strangling an 89-year-old woman in her home in Co Tipperary two years ago, was instructed by gardaí to leave the house six months before her death. Hasan Ali Gori, aged 52, originally from Chad, has pleaded not guilty to murdering Josephine 'Josie' Ray in the bedroom of her home in Nenagh on 4 August 2024. The accused was living in the home of the pensioner, as he was in a relationship with her daughter, Mary Ray, who has an intellectual disability. Gardaí who were on patrol in Nenagh gave evidence of calling to an address in St Joseph’s Park on 13 March 2024, after they received a report of a domestic incident. The jury at the Central Criminal Court heard that while gardaí were speaking to Josephine Ray and members of her family, a phone call was received by a family member and put on loudspeaker. Garda Jack Walker told the court that he heard an argument between Mary Ray and her partner over the phone.

stories.title: Stokell enters suspension after medication breach
stories.summary: Ireland cricketer Rebecca Stokell has accepted a voluntary ban for what Cricket Ireland described as "an inadvertent breach of the reporting requirements around the use of prescription medication". The International Cricket Council (ICC) said a sample Stokell provided during the Women's T20 World Cup on 23 June returned "an adverse finding for a specified substance". On Monday, Cricket Ireland confirmed that Stokell has entered into voluntary suspension - effective 23 October - while she awaits the outcome of the investigation by the ICC. In a statement, Cricket Ireland said: "While the breach was unintentional and the substance acknowledged as non-performance enhancing, Stokell has admitted she did not comply with the regulations and accepts the likely outcome will be a suspension from the game." Stokell said: "I fully accept my mistake and have voluntarily entered into a period of suspension ahead of the findings being returned. "While this was not performance related in any way, I understand that I am responsible for following the Anti-Doping Guidelines and I hope that I can be back playing for Ireland as soon as possible."

stories.title: Adventurer returns home after 28-year trek across globe
stories.summary: Adventurer Karl Bushby has made his final stop in his home city of Hull this morning following a 28-year walk from South America. Mr Bushby, now 57, set off from the southern end of Chile in 1998, when he was 28, vowing to walk all the way home without using any form of motorised transport. Finally home, he was greeted by hundreds of well-wishers outside the City Hall in Hull. "There has never been a welcome home quite like this," Mr Bushby said. "This is absolute madness. After 28 years, you couldn't ask for more than this. This is the last, last few steps. "I didn't do this alone. It was a big team. The biggest team - Earth.
